Ah, the freedom of a blank page—where to begin? Maybe with the way sunlight slants through my window in the late afternoon, turning dust motes into tiny constellations. Or the way my cat, a small tyrant with fur like storm clouds, kneads my lap as if she’s trying to summon bread from my thighs. (She’s not wrong; I *do* rise under her paws.)

I’ve been thinking about the quiet rebellions of everyday life. The way people hum to themselves in grocery store lines, or how a stranger’s laugh can make you smile when you didn’t even know you were frowning. There’s something subversive in those small, unscripted moments—they’re proof that we’re not just cogs in the machine, even when the machine insists we are.

Or maybe it’s the way stories work. How a single sentence can crack open a world, or how a character’s silence can say more than their words. I love the idea that every person is walking around with a novel’s worth of untold history in their bones. What if we all just… started talking? Not to perform, not to impress, but to say: *Here’s the thing that keeps me up at night. Here’s the joke that makes me snort-laugh. Here’s the memory I’ve never shared because it feels too fragile.*

(Then again, maybe that’s terrifying. Maybe we’re all just pretending we’re not terrified.)

I’ve been listening to a lot of old folk music lately—the kind with fiddles that sound like heartbeats and lyrics that feel like they’ve been passed down through generations. There’s a line in one song: *"The river don’t care where it’s going, it just keeps on rolling."* I think about that a lot. How much of life is just… rolling? Not in a passive way, but in a *trusting the current* way. Not fighting the flow, but not letting it carry you under either.

What about you? What’s something small that’s been occupying your mind? A half-remembered dream? A song that’s been stuck in your head for days? A question you’re too afraid to ask out loud? (I won’t tell.)

Or maybe you’re just here for the cat stories. In which case: *She once stole an entire slice of pizza off my plate while I was mid-conversation. The audacity.*
